title: Constructing and explaining an organisation chart

blocks.heading: Constructing and explaining an organisation chart
blocks.text: To draw a simple organisation chart, identify the most senior position, group positions at the correct levels and join each subordinate to the position it reports to directly. Use role titles rather than a list of names without jobs. Do not connect neighbouring roles merely because they are at the same level: a connecting line would imply a reporting relationship not stated. Keep direct spans distinguishable from all lower-level staff. The chart makes formal authority visible and helps a new worker identify a supervisor, but it does not show the quality of management or the informal communication network. Check the finished chart against each reporting fact. A line accidentally bypassing a supervisor changes the structure even if all job titles are present.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text:
Omano Supplies has an owner-manager. Production, sales and finance heads each report to the owner-manager. Workers A and B report to the production head; a sales assistant reports to the sales head; an accounts clerk reports to the finance head. ![Omano Supplies reporting structure](diagrams/omano-reporting.png)

Place the owner-manager at the top, the three heads at the second level and their direct staff at the third. The owner-manager’s span is three; the production head’s span is two. There are three levels. The chain from Worker A to the owner-manager goes through the production head, not the sales head.
